qt: to the Commission Marcin Sypniewski (ESN) Subject:

On 1 October 2026, representatives of the German organisation BUND, the Coalition Clean Baltic and the Lebensraum Vorpommern initiative presented Commissioner Jessica Roswall with a petition demanding a ban on oil and gas extraction in the Baltic Sea. This action also targets the planned exploitation of the Wolin East field within the Polish maritime territory. Utilising domestic resources could bolster Poland’s energy security and reduce its reliance on imports. Article 194(2) TFEU protects the right of Member States to determine the conditions for exploiting their own energy resources and exercising this right requires compliance with environmental regulations. Environmental protection procedures should be grounded in an assessment of genuine risks rather than being used to force Poland into abandoning extraction under pressure from foreign organisations. In light of the above: 1.
What steps has the Commission taken since receiving the petition, and has it initiated proceedings or contacted the Polish authorities regarding the Wolin East project?
Does it acknowledge Poland’s right to exploit its own resources in compliance with EU law, and is there a legal basis for introducing a blanket ban on oil and gas extraction in the Baltic Sea?

Does Germany’s participation in the cross-border environmental impact assessment grant it the right, as a neighbouring Member State, to block a Polish investment project, and if so, on what legal basis, or does it merely grant the right to obtain information, participate in consultations, and submit comments that the competent Polish authorities must consider when taking a decision?
